source.original_text: In the source construction n is sufficiently large and h=floor((log n)^(1/3)/32). Set K=2^(74(h+1)), P=2^(64(h+1)), S_i=Σ_{j=0}^{h−i}K^j, and a_i,p=1/[p^4 S_i² sqrt((h−i+1)log(2PS_i))]. For 0≤i≤h and even 4≤p≤P, take deterministic unit directions u_i,…,u_h and the ordered tensor ψ_i=u_i⊗u_(i+1)^⊗K⊗⋯⊗u_h^⊗K^(h−i). A standard Gaussian coefficient tensor Ξ_i,p in real Euclidean dimension n^(pS_i) defines F_i,p=√n a_i,p⟨Ξ_i,p,ψ_i^⊗p⟩. At each fixed direction tuple, F_i,p has law N(0,n a_i,p²). The isolated formal identity is valid for every positive n and natural h; joint independence and the degree-summed field are not covered here.

let F := fun (n : ℕ+) (h : ℕ) (i : Fin (h + 1))
    (p : {p : ℕ // Even p ∧ 4 ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 ^ (64 * (h + 1))})
    (u : Fin (h - i.val + 1) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n.val))
    (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ
      ((Fin p.val × (Σ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1),
        Fin ((2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val))) → Fin n.val)) ↦
  let S : ℕ := ∑ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1), (2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val
  let a : ℝ := 1 / ((p.val : ℝ) ^ 4 * (S : ℝ) ^ 2 *
    Real.sqrt ((h - i.val + 1 : ℕ) * Real.log (2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (64 * (h + 1)) * S)))
  Real.sqrt n.val * a * ∑ c, ξ c * ∏ s, u s.2.1 (c s)
;
∀ (n : ℕ+) (h : ℕ) (i : Fin (h + 1))
    (p : {p : ℕ // Even p ∧ 4 ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 ^ (64 * (h + 1))})
    (u : Fin (h - i.val + 1) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n.val))
    (hu : ∀ j, ‖u j‖ = 1),
    let S : ℕ := ∑ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1), (2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val
    let a : ℝ := 1 / ((p.val : ℝ) ^ 4 * (S : ℝ) ^ 2 *
      Real.sqrt ((h - i.val + 1 : ℕ) * Real.log (2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (64 * (h + 1)) * S)))
    HasLaw (F n h i p u)
      (gaussianReal 0 (((n.val : ℝ) * a ^ 2).toNNReal)) (stdGaussian _)

blind_reconstruction.text: Claim with a locally defined function. Let n be a positive integer, h a nonnegative integer, i an integer with 0 <= i <= h, and p an even integer satisfying 4 <= p <= Q, where Q = 2^(64(h+1)). Put m = h-i+1 (the displayed natural subtraction is truncated), B = 2^(74(h+1)), S = sum_{j=0}^{m-1} B^j, and a = 1 / [p^4 S^2 sqrt(m log(2 Q S))], with natural-number quantities interpreted as reals in this formula and log the natural logarithm. Set T = {(r,j,k) : 0 <= r < p, 0 <= j < m, 0 <= k < B^j}, and let C be the set of all functions c:T -> {0,...,n-1}. For a deterministic tuple u = (u_0,...,u_{m-1}) in (R^n)^m and a coefficient vector xi in R^C, define F(n,h,i,p,u,xi) = sqrt(n) a sum_{c in C} xi_c product_{r=0}^{p-1} product_{j=0}^{m-1} product_{k=0}^{B^j-1} (u_j)_{c(r,j,k)}. The claim is that, for every such n,h,i,p and every such u satisfying ||u_j||_2 = 1 for every j, the map xi -> F(n,h,i,p,u,xi) is almost-everywhere measurable under the standard Gaussian probability measure on R^C, and its pushforward of that measure is the real Gaussian law with mean 0 and variance max(n a^2,0), equivalently variance n a^2. Here the standard Gaussian on R^C has mean zero and identity covariance. There are p S slots and n^(p S) coefficient coordinates; u_j occurs in p B^j slots. Only xi is random. This specifies a scalar law for each fixed admissible deterministic tuple u; it does not assert a simultaneous bound, a joint law over different tuples, or a probability event uniform over u.

import Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.Multivariate
import Mathlib.Probability.HasLaw
import Mathlib.Data.PNat.Basic

/-!
# The actual Gaussian angular degree component

Zhou–Suzuki, arXiv:2611.05813v1 (CC BY 4.0), Section 4.1.1, Eq. (14)–(15).
Tensor coordinates are indexed by a choice in each repeated tensor slot. This
retains the ordered tensor, its multiplicities and the exact source amplitude.
The law is for deterministic unit directions under one actual standard Gaussian
coefficient block. Joint coefficient independence, degree summation, radial
cutoffs and conditional level iteration are separate obligations.

The isolated identity permits every positive dimension and natural depth; it
does not assert hard-family admissibility outside the source parameter regime.
The literal polynomial extends to arbitrary directions, but its Gaussian law
below uses only the source sphere domain.
-/

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped BigOperators

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SlcLsiQueryComplexity.AngularDegree

/-- The literal Eq. (15) degree component, including the Eq. (14) amplitude.
The tensor slots select a copy of `psi`, then a trailing block and repetition.
Only its restriction to unit directions is used by the source-law theorem. -/
noncomputable def angularDegreeComponent (n : ℕ+) (h : ℕ) (i : Fin (h + 1))
    (p : {p : ℕ // Even p ∧ 4 ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 ^ (64 * (h + 1))})
    (u : Fin (h - i.val + 1) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n.val))
    (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ
      ((Fin p.val × (Σ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1),
        Fin ((2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val))) → Fin n.val)) : ℝ :=
  let S : ℕ := ∑ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1), (2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val
  let a : ℝ := 1 / ((p.val : ℝ) ^ 4 * (S : ℝ) ^ 2 *
    Real.sqrt ((h - i.val + 1 : ℕ) * Real.log (2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (64 * (h + 1)) * S)))
  Real.sqrt n.val * a * ∑ c, ξ c * ∏ s, u s.2.1 (c s)

private abbrev TensorSlots (h : ℕ) (i : Fin (h + 1)) (p : ℕ) :=
  Fin p × (Σ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1), Fin ((2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val))

private noncomputable def tensorFeature (n : ℕ+) (h : ℕ) (i : Fin (h + 1)) (p : ℕ)
    (u : Fin (h - i.val + 1) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n.val)) :
    EuclideanSpace ℝ (TensorSlots h i p → Fin n.val) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 fun c ↦ ∏ s, u s.2.1 (c s)

private theorem tensorFeature_norm_sq (n : ℕ+) (h : ℕ) (i : Fin (h + 1)) (p : ℕ)
    (u : Fin (h - i.val + 1) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n.val))
    (hu : ∀ j, ‖u j‖ = 1) : ‖tensorFeature n h i p u‖ ^ 2 = 1 := by
  rw [EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq]
  change (∑ c : TensorSlots h i p → Fin n.val,
    (∏ s : TensorSlots h i p, u s.2.1 (c s)) ^ 2) = 1
  simp_rw [← Finset.prod_pow]
  rw [← Fintype.prod_sum (fun (s : TensorSlots h i p) (k : Fin n.val) ↦
    (u s.2.1 k) ^ 2)]
  simp_rw [← EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq, hu]
  simp

/-- At fixed unit directions the actual Gaussian tensor polynomial has the
source centered normal law with variance `n * a²`. This proves measurability and
the law; neither a Gaussian-law witness nor tensor normalization is assumed. -/
theorem angularDegreeComponent_hasLaw (n : ℕ+) (h : ℕ) (i : Fin (h + 1))
    (p : {p : ℕ // Even p ∧ 4 ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 ^ (64 * (h + 1))})
    (u : Fin (h - i.val + 1) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n.val))
    (hu : ∀ j, ‖u j‖ = 1) :
    let S : ℕ := ∑ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1), (2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val
    let a : ℝ := 1 / ((p.val : ℝ) ^ 4 * (S : ℝ) ^ 2 *
      Real.sqrt ((h - i.val + 1 : ℕ) * Real.log (2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (64 * (h + 1)) * S)))
    HasLaw (angularDegreeComponent n h i p u)
      (gaussianReal 0 (((n.val : ℝ) * a ^ 2).toNNReal)) (stdGaussian _) := by
  let S : ℕ := ∑ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1), (2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val
  let a : ℝ := 1 / ((p.val : ℝ) ^ 4 * (S : ℝ) ^ 2 *
    Real.sqrt ((h - i.val + 1 : ℕ) * Real.log (2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (64 * (h + 1)) * S)))
  let L : StrongDual ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (TensorSlots h i p.val → Fin n.val)) :=
    (Real.sqrt n.val * a) • innerSL ℝ (tensorFeature n h i p.val u)
  change HasLaw (angularDegreeComponent n h i p u)
    (gaussianReal 0 (((n.val : ℝ) * a ^ 2).toNNReal)) (stdGaussian _)
  have hL : (fun ξ ↦ L ξ) = angularDegreeComponent n h i p u := by
    funext ξ
    change (Real.sqrt n.val * a) * inner ℝ (tensorFeature n h i p.val u) ξ =
      (Real.sqrt n.val * a) * ∑ c, ξ c * ∏ s, u s.2.1 (c s)
    congr 1
  have hnorm : ‖L‖ ^ 2 = (n.val : ℝ) * a ^ 2 := by
    simp only [L, norm_smul, innerSL_apply_norm, mul_pow, Real.norm_eq_abs, sq_abs]
    rw [tensorFeature_norm_sq n h i p.val u hu, mul_one,
      Real.sq_sqrt (Nat.cast_nonneg n.val)]
  rw [← hL]
  refine ⟨L.continuous.aemeasurable, ?_⟩
  rw [IsGaussian.map_eq_gaussianReal, integral_strongDual_stdGaussian,
    variance_dual_stdGaussian, hnorm]

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SlcLsiQueryComplexity.AngularDegree

formulae.label: Ordered tensor and component
formulae.tex: \psi_i=u_i\otimes u_{i+1}^{\otimes K}\otimes\cdots\otimes u_h^{\otimes K^{h-i}},\qquad F_{i,p}^{\Xi}(u)=\sqrt n\,a_{i,p}\langle\Xi_{i,p},\psi_i(u)^{\otimes p}\rangle.

assumptions: n is a positive integer, h a nonnegative integer, 0≤i≤h, and p is even with 4≤p≤P.
The trailing directions u_i,…,u_h are fixed deterministic unit vectors in real Euclidean n-space.
The coefficient block has its unconditioned standard Gaussian probability law; it is not conditioned on admissibility.

lesson.title: The angular component has its stated Gaussian law
assumptions: n is a positive integer, h a nonnegative integer, 0≤i≤h, and p is even with 4≤p≤P.
The trailing directions u_i,…,u_h are fixed deterministic unit vectors in real Euclidean n-space.
The coefficient block has its unconditioned standard Gaussian probability law; it is not conditioned on admissibility.
The paper fixes sufficiently large n and h=floor((log n)^(1/3)/32). The isolated identity below is proved for every positive n and natural h; this does not extend hard-family admissibility.
lesson.statement: For the displayed source parameters and any fixed unit directions, the literal component F_i,p evaluated under its standard Gaussian coefficient block is a centered real Gaussian with variance n a_i,p². Its measurability and distribution identity are proved, not assumed.
lesson.reader_note: The tensor formula and every constant are available in the definition below. Random or adaptively selected directions are not covered by this pointwise statement.

steps.title: Unit directions give a unit tensor
steps.text: Square each feature entry, sum over all coordinate choices, and distribute the finite product of sums. Each inner sum is the squared Euclidean norm of a participating direction, hence one. Repeated copies are essential multiplicities, but do not change this unit norm.
steps.lean: tensorFeature_norm_sq expands EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq, moves the square inside the finite product, and applies Fintype.prod_sum. Only hu, the source unit-direction condition, is supplied.

steps.title: Use the actual Gaussian linear functional
steps.text: For fixed directions define L(ξ)=√n a_i,p⟨q,ξ⟩. The coordinate formula identifies the component exactly with L. This is a continuous linear map, hence measurable. Under the standard Gaussian block, its mean is zero and its variance is the squared operator norm.
steps.lean: innerSL makes the inner product a continuous linear functional; hL identifies it with the literal polynomial. Mathlib supplies integral_strongDual_stdGaussian, variance_dual_stdGaussian and IsGaussian.map_eq_gaussianReal.

steps.title: Compute the variance and package the law
steps.text: The norm of the inner-product functional is the feature norm. Its square is one, and (√n)²=n because n≥1. Thus the variance is exactly n a_i,p². HasLaw packages a.e. measurability with equality of the pushforward probability measure; it is the conclusion, not an input.
steps.formula: \begin{gathered}\|L\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2=(\sqrt n\,a_{i,p})^2\|q\|_2^2=n a_{i,p}^2,\\ (\xi\mapsto F_{i,p}^{\xi}(u))_\#\mathcal N(0,I_C)=\mathcal N(0,n a_{i,p}^2).\end{gathered}
steps.lean: norm_smul and innerSL_apply_norm reduce the variance to the proved tensor norm; Real.sq_sqrt removes the square root. The nonnegative variance conversion is exact, as the focused test also checks.

lesson.lean_statement: HasLaw f μ P means AEMeasurable f P and P.map f=μ. Here P is the concrete stdGaussian on the tensor-coordinate Euclidean space. There is no assumed Gaussian law, independence, feature norm or integrability premise.
lesson.lean_proof: Three private providers name slots, construct the tensor feature and prove its norm. The public proof then identifies the linear map and invokes pinned Mathlib Gaussian facts. They receive no separate leaf credit. Parameter positivity and coordinate dimension are also checked by universal examples in the focused test.
lesson.dependency_notes: The new ASTIS object is the literal source polynomial; Gaussian linear-law infrastructure is reused from Mathlib. Future degree-sum and conditional applications are planned consumers, not existing Lean call edges.
